Run a resumable batch of web entries and analyse confirmed observations

Source: R/web_entry.R
web_entry_run.Rd

web_entry_run() enters the observations of a batch built with web_entry_batch() into the remote web application and confirms each one by reading it back. It is safe to call again after an interruption:

  • every key is read back before anything is saved, so a record that was saved by an earlier run (whose local receipt was lost) is adopted instead of being entered again;

  • a record already holding different values under the same key is reported as a conflict and is never overwritten;

  • when the outcome of an earlier save is unknown, the record is verified rather than resubmitted;

  • a save is only treated as confirmed when a readback shows the fields agree with the batch; the adapter's return value, including an apparent success message, is never treated as confirmation.

Only when every row is confirmed by a readback made during this run are the confirmed observations passed to specify() and fit() with the batch's original formula. Otherwise, or if the analysis or writing the analysis fails, the previous usable analysis is kept and reported instead.

Usage

web_entry_run(
  batch,
  browser = NULL,
  max_attempts = 3L,
  state_dir = NULL,
  analyze = TRUE
)

# S3 method for class 'infer_web_entry'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

batch

A batch built with web_entry_batch().

browser

A logged-in browser handle. Defaults to the handle supplied to web_entry_batch().

max_attempts

The maximum cumulative number of save attempts per row.

state_dir

Directory holding persisted progress. Defaults to the batch's state_dir.

analyze

Whether to analyse and fit the batch when it is fully confirmed.

x

An object of class infer_web_entry, as returned by web_entry_run() or web_entry_verify().

...

Unused.

Value

An object of class infer_web_entry, a list with components:

  • fingerprint: the batch fingerprint.

  • receipts: a tibble with one receipt per row: key, status, confirmed, remote_saved, attempts, confirmed_at, values, and detail.

  • complete: whether every row is confirmed by a readback from this run.

  • included: the observations actually included in the analysis (those read back from the remote application), or those of the previous usable analysis when no current one is available.

  • coefficients: the native fit() coefficients for the batch formula, for the analysis reported in analysis$status.

  • analysis: a list with status ("current", "stale", "failed", or "none"), reason, completed_at, persisted, previous, and, when a current fit could not be kept, computed.

x, invisibly.

See also

web_entry_batch(), web_entry_verify(), web_entry_receipts()
